docs.title: What Lantern is
docs.text:
What Lantern is

Lantern turns one device on your Wi-Fi into a local content server. Anyone on the same network opens the address the host prints, in a plain browser, and reads the library. No internet is used at any point, and nothing leaves the host unless you export it.

The host is a single Node file with no dependencies. The client is one page with no build step.

docs.title: Make a pack
docs.text:
Make a pack

A pack is one JSON file. Give it an id, a title and a list of documents, each with a path, a title and its text content.

{ "id": "my-pack", "title": "My Pack", "docs": [ { "path": "notes.html", "title": "Notes", "content": "<h1>Notes</h1>" } ] }

Import it from the Packs card. Lantern records a SHA-256 and the byte length of every file it writes, and checks them again each time it loads. A pack whose files no longer match is quarantined and reported, never served with pages missing.

docs.title: How search ranks
docs.text:
How search ranks

Search runs over an index built from every document in every pack, on the host. Words are matched case-insensitively and common English stop words are ignored.

A document that contains the whole query as a phrase outranks documents that merely contain its words, which is what makes a search for a phrase that occurs in exactly one document return that document first. Removing a pack removes its documents from the index immediately.
